chunks: From him, from al-Nadr, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When you slaughter an animal and there is a complete offspring in its womb, then its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother. If it is not complete, then do not eat it."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating an animal if a fully developed or undeveloped fetus is found in its womb during slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of 'slaughter within slaughter,' establishing that a fully formed fetus (tām) inherits the mother’s ritual status, thereby rendering it halal without separate slaughter. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that the embryo is an integral part of the mother’s body until it reaches a stage of distinct development, contrasting with some Sunni schools that require separate slaughter or consider it distinct from the moment of birth. The distinction hinges on the biological and legal definition of 'tām' (complete/perfect), ensuring that only fully developed offspring are treated as independent entities for dietary laws.
